correctness.rationale: A covering Italian function is exactly an Italian function whose positive support is a vertex cover, so its zero set is independent. In a complete multipartite graph, every independent set lies in one part. Thus either there are no zeros, contributing \(z^N(1+z)^N\), or a unique part contains all zeros. All vertices outside that part are then positive. If there are at least two outside vertices, their minimum total label is already two, so the Italian constraint is automatic; if there is exactly one outside vertex, it must receive label \(2\). This proves the stated \(B_qT_{n_i}\) decomposition and \(\gamma_{cI}=\max\{2,N-M\}\). A fresh independent exhaustive replay through order six reproduced the literal vertex-cover/Italian definition and every coefficient.
residual_risks: The theorem is for connected complete multipartite graphs; isolated or disconnected cases need separate treatment.

originality.rationale: Covering Italian domination is equivalent to the earlier outer-independent Italian definition because a positive support is a vertex cover exactly when its zero set is independent. Fan et al. introduce that same parameter and study bounds, extremal trees, and vertex-cover relations. Khodkar et al.'s full preprint studies the covering formulation, complexity, bounds, and equality with vertex-cover parameters. Those scalar results substantially cover the minimum-value corollary, but their inspected full texts do not state the complete-multipartite all-function classification or the weight enumerator. Current Resultary searches likewise found no prior exact census.
residual_risks: A later paper may use only the outer-independent Italian name and contain an unindexed class-specific census; none was found in current searches.

value.rationale: Covering/outer-independent Italian domination is an established labeling invariant tied directly to vertex covers. Counting all feasible functions by weight is a natural refinement, and complete multipartite graphs expose a clean zero-set structure that yields a closed polynomial and exact boundary at a one-vertex complement. The scalar minimum is treated as largely prior; the accepted value lies in the full function distribution.
residual_risks: The structural proof is short because independent sets in complete multipartite graphs are especially rigid.

scientific_limitations: The theorem is for connected complete multipartite graphs; isolated or disconnected cases need separate treatment.
